description: Reduce critical preloader-blocking frames from 150 to 50 for 1st-vdo, and add a service worker for frame sequence caching
steps: In src/hooks/useSequencesPreload.ts, add a new optional field to SequenceConfig called `criticalCount` (number, optional). When a critical sequence has `criticalCount` set, only load that many thumbnail frames (evenly spaced across the range 0 to count-1) before marking the preloader as ready. The remaining thumbnails should load in the background after ready=true, then full-res loads after all thumbnails are in.

In src/components/HomeExperience.tsx, set `criticalCount: 50` on the 1st-vdo sequence config. This means only 50 evenly-spaced thumbnails out of 150 load before dismissing the preloader (frames 0, 3, 6, 9, ... every 3rd frame). The other 100 thumbnails load immediately after in background.

Update the useSequencesPreload hook logic so that: (a) For critical sequences with criticalCount, calculate which frame indices are 'critical' (evenly spaced). Load only those thumbs and track progress against criticalCount. (b) Once criticalCount thumbs are loaded, set ready=true and report 100% progress. (c) Immediately begin loading the remaining (non-critical) thumbnails in background. (d) Once ALL thumbnails are loaded, begin full-res swap as before.

Create a service worker at public/sw.js that: (a) On install, does NOT precache anything (to avoid blocking). (b) On fetch, intercepts requests for frame sequences (URLs matching /1st-vdo/, /2nd-vdo/, /3rd-vdo/, /4th-vdo/ and their -thumb variants). (c) Uses a cache-first strategy: check CacheStorage first, if hit return cached response; if miss, fetch from network, put in cache, and return. (d) Uses a named cache like 'frame-sequences-v1'. (e) For all other requests, falls through to network (does not interfere with Next.js routing).

Register the service worker from the app. Create src/hooks/useServiceWorker.ts that registers /sw.js on mount (only in production, check process.env.NODE_ENV or just always register). Call this hook from src/components/HomeExperience.tsx (or src/app/layout.tsx).
Verify the build passes and all files are correctly wired.
acceptance_criteria: The preloader dismisses after loading only 50 thumbnails (not 150) for the 1st-vdo critical sequence
The remaining 100 thumbnails for 1st-vdo load in background after preloader dismisses
Full-res frame loading still happens after all thumbnails are loaded
A service worker at public/sw.js implements cache-first strategy for frame sequences
The service worker is registered from the React app
npm run build passes without errors
The ImageSequencePlayer still works correctly - it reads from imagesRef which will have frames populated progressively
verification: Run `npm run build` and confirm it succeeds without errors
Read src/hooks/useSequencesPreload.ts and verify criticalCount logic only tracks 50 frames for progress
Read public/sw.js and verify cache-first strategy for frame URLs
Read the service worker registration hook and verify it registers sw.js
findings: Build passes cleanly. The evenly-spaced index formula Math.round((j * (count-1)) / (criticalCount-1)) produces exactly 50 unique indices for criticalCount=50, count=150 (every 3rd frame: 0, 3, 6, ..., 147). Service worker registered on window load event to avoid competing with initial page load.
